Doge Jewish Cemetery Two

Jewish Cemetery · Döge, Hungary

Not demolished. This second of Döge's two Jewish cemetery entries in the source database (unlike the other Döge record, this one has genuine, non-duplicated content) confirms the site was in use from at least 1870 to 1901, per cadastral maps, before a road later divided it, apparently destroying part of the grounds. The village's first Jews were recorded in an 1770 census (4 residents, including stillman Jakab Herskovics), growing to 117 by 1870 before steadily declining to just 17 by 1930. An 1848 document records the cemetery covering 2 acres. By 1949, no Jews remained in Döge. Eyewitness accounts describe descendants regularly visiting through the 1950s, when a couple dozen gravestones still stood; today the stones are scattered, and some village buildings reportedly incorporate blocks bearing Hebrew inscriptions.
